- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (≤ 0.10), model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast for 7–14 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not exceed 2–3% above prior peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-cycle corrections; adjust downward by 1–4% in final 5–7 days if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
